clinician.final_diagnosis: Post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis (PSGN) with concurrent posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES)
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 15-year-old previously healthy male presented with a 7-day history of fever, headache, projectile vomiting, transient blurry vision (24 hours duration), and two episodes of generalized seizures with postictal confusion lasting 3-5 minutes each. On admission, vital signs revealed significantly elevated blood pressure of 150/100 mmHg (99th percentile for age) with normal heart rate of 82 bpm. Neurological examination was largely unremarkable except for decreased visual acuity of the left eye; fundoscopy was normal. Laboratory investigations at admission demonstrated leukocytosis, positive dengue IgM antibodies, decreased complement 3, elevated anti-streptolysin (ASO) titers, uremia, hematuria, and proteinuria. MRI brain imaging revealed symmetrical enhancement of superficial and deep watershed areas predominantly in the occipital and temporal regions, consistent with PRES. The patient was diagnosed with post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis based on the constellation of fever, elevated ASO titers, decreased C3 complement, proteinuria, and hematuria. Treatment was initiated with ceftriaxone for antimicrobial coverage and amlodipine for blood pressure management. By day 6 post-admission, the patient became asymptomatic with only minimal hematuria persisting. Repeat MRI brain at 3 weeks post-admission demonstrated complete resolution of the hyperintense lesions, confirming resolution of PRES.
